title: String Splitting for Domain Logic Extraction
pattern: Parsing and pulling out domain properties by performing raw string operations (slicing, regex matches, or splitting) inside core business logic.
why_bad: It couples business logic to raw string patterns, leading to duplicate parsing algorithms, unhandled edge cases (e.g., malformed email inputs causing panics), and brittle refactoring.
detection: Slicing or string parsing operations (`.split()`, `.find()`, regex captures) acting on string identifiers within domain services.
counterexample: Parsing raw JSON payloads or command-line strings at the system boundary (e.g., HTTP controllers or DTO translation layers).
fix:
Perform parsing exactly once at the boundary, converting the input into a strongly-typed struct.
```rust
struct EmailAddress {
    username: String,
    domain: String,
}
```
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design* by John K. Ousterhout (p. 45); *Domain Modeling made Functional* (p. 110).
